members.label: ds:Signature
members.note: POSITION NOT STATED BY CONFLUENCE. Page 7766254 says only that the response is signed 'Sign the Assertion way', i.e. the signature covers the saml:Assertion. It does not say where inside the Assertion the ds:Signature element sits, and the published skeleton is explicitly the version 'without signature tag'. This member is placed after saml:Issuer because that is where SAML 2.0 Core's schema puts it — an EXTERNAL fact, not a NPHIES one. Do not report a signature elsewhere in the Assertion as a NPHIES violation.
members.guidance: Signing itself is OUT OF SCOPE of the Confluence spec: 'To sign SAML responses, we use a Signing SAML tool that simplifies the process.' / 'Using this tool, you can paste an unsigned SAML Response, then sign it using the public and private X.509 certificates in the selected "mode."' The page links an external tool (https://www.samltool.com/sign_response.php). No canonicalization method, digest method, signature method, transform or KeyInfo rule is stated anywhere in these pages, so none is modelled. That the signature is REQUIRED is stated elsewhere: page 7766173 'The Identity Provider responsible for issuing the signed SAML response' and page 7766210 'Oracle IAM validate SAML signature.'

notes: NO OFFICIAL GOLDEN SAMPLE EXISTS for saml-sso. Every member of this structure rests on Confluence prose and on one literal XML skeleton published on page 7766254; nothing here has been checked against a message NPHIES actually accepted. `verifiedAgainstSample` is false and the structure confidence is "medium" for that reason alone — the skeleton itself is unambiguous.

DIRECTION. This is `direction: "request"` even though the XML element is called samlp:Response: the hospital's EMR/HIS generates and SENDS it. Page 7766210: 'EMR/HIS application will generate SAML response.' In SAML terms the EMR/HIS is the Identity Provider and NPHIES is the Service Provider.

The skeleton on page 7766254 is published WITHOUT the signature tag ('SAML Sample XML (without signature tag)'). A real message carries a ds:Signature over the Assertion; see the ds:Signature member, whose position inside the Assertion is NOT stated by Confluence.

Confluence's auto-linker destroyed the angle brackets of seven opening tags in the skeleton (samlp:Status, saml:Subject, saml:AudienceRestriction, saml:Audience, saml:AuthnContext, saml:AuthnContextClassRef, saml:AttributeStatement). Each such member carries a `note` saying so, and `skeletonRepairs` lists every repair. All seven are certain, because the matching CLOSING tag survived on the following line.
The skeleton is the ONA-environment sample. Destination, Recipient and Audience are per-environment and MUST be swapped for the target environment; see `environments`.
Every literal value in the skeleton's four variable slots (Deemaalqassem, 1095650865, 10000300236625, 30000999999999) is sample data, not a constant.
@SessionNotOnOrAfter in the skeleton (2023-10-11T08:55:32Z) predates its own @AuthnInstant (2025-04-22T08:14:46Z) — stale sample data on the page, not a rule.
family is "saml", which MessageStructure.family (SpecFamily) does not admit today; see `compilerNotes`. All locators are `cdaXPath`, whose familyOfLocator() is "cda".

knownGaps.gap: Page 7766254 states only that the response is signed 'Sign the Assertion way' and hands the job to an external tool (https://www.samltool.com/sign_response.php). No ds:Signature internals are specified anywhere: no canonicalization method, digest method, signature method, transform list, reference URI convention, KeyInfo/X509Data requirement, and no statement of where inside the Assertion the element sits.
knownGaps.effect: The ds:Signature member records ONLY that a signature exists and that it covers the Assertion. Its children are deliberately empty. A checker must not report a signature's internals as conforming or non-conforming against this structure.

knownGaps.gap: The page lists exactly ONE signing option — 'Sign the Assertion way' — as a single bullet under the plural phrase 'A SAML Response can be signed in:'. The plural wording suggests a second option (Response-level signing) was intended and is missing from the page.
knownGaps.effect: Only Assertion-level signing is modelled. Response-level signing is neither required nor forbidden here.
knownGaps.resolvedBy: Ask NPHIES whether a Response-level signature is also accepted.

compilerNotes.what: `MessageStructure.family` is typed `SpecFamily = "hl7v2" | "fhir" | "cda" | "xds"`, which has no "saml" member. `UseCaseSummary.family` ALREADY admits "saml" and its own comment says '`saml` appears here although it is not a `SpecFamily`: it has no field tables.'
compilerNotes.chosen: This patch emits `"family": "saml"`, matching UseCaseSummary and the truth, rather than mislabelling the message as CDA or XDS.
optionsForCompiler: Widen SpecFamily (or MessageStructure.family) to include "saml" — the smallest honest change, and consistent with what UseCaseSummary already does.
Keep SpecFamily as-is and let the compiler map "saml" -> a nullable/extended field on the structure record.
compilerNotes.doNot: Do NOT set family to "cda". Locators here are cdaXPath because that is the XML locator kind the contract offers, but the message is not a CDA document and must not be labelled one. Note that familyOfLocator() on any locator in this structure returns "cda" — a consistency check that compares structure.family with familyOfLocator will fire on saml-sso and should be exempted rather than 'fixed' by relabelling the structure.

compilerNotes.what: `EnvelopeSpec` is a union of hl7v2Message | fhirBundle | cdaDocument | soapEnvelope. There is no SAML kind, and `MessageEncoding` DOES already include "saml-xml" — so the encoding was anticipated and the envelope was not.
compilerNotes.chosen: `structure.envelope` is null. The envelope facts (root element, required namespaces, signature placement) are carried in this patch's `samlEnvelope` and `namespaces`, plus as real members of the tree, so nothing is lost and nothing is faked into a soapEnvelope.
compilerNotes.proposedShape: see `samlEnvelope.proposedEnvelopeSpec` — adopt only if structure.ts is widened.

compilerNotes.what: `SpecRole` (data | structural | container | omit) is declared on `SpecNode`, not on `StructureMemberBase`. saml-sso has no field tables and therefore no SpecNodes, so there is nowhere in the contract to put the role.
compilerNotes.chosen: Every element member in this patch carries `role` (a valid SpecRole value) as an additive field. TypeScript's excess-property check does not apply to JSON-parsed data, so the bundle still satisfies StructureElement. The four data slots additionally carry `variableSlot`.
optionsForCompiler: Carry `role` through onto the structure member (what a UI asking 'what must I actually build?' needs).
Synthesise one SpecNode per member from these fields and point at them with specRefs — more faithful to the contract, more machinery.

compilerNotes.what: Whether SAML warrants a new locator kind.
compilerNotes.chosen: `cdaXPath` is used throughout, as instructed. It fits without strain: `path` + `relativeTo` + `attribute` + `predicate` express every address in this tree, and locatorKey() yields unique, stable keys (the two saml:Issuer elements differ by relativeTo, and the two saml:Attribute elements by predicate).
compilerNotes.recommendation: No new locator kind is needed for saml-sso. If one is ever added for XML generally, the honest move is to RENAME cdaXPath to something family-neutral rather than add a parallel kind — the same argument applies to the SOAP/XDS structures, which already use cdaXPath for non-CDA XML.

compilerNotes.what: The NPHIES usage legend (page 171278410) is a TABLE legend. saml-sso has no table, so no cell ever said M/R/O for any of these members.
compilerNotes.chosen: Every member carries usage [{usage: "R", min: 1, max: 1, raw: {usage: null, cardinality: null}}]. `raw` is null on purpose: there is no cell to quote. The code "R" is DERIVED from presence in the single published skeleton, not read from a source. A checker should say 'required by the published SAML skeleton' rather than 'required per the usage table'.

compilerNotes.what: What the manifest needs so gate blocker 1 actually closes.

confidenceReason: The element tree, its order, its attribute names and every fixed urn value come from one LITERAL XML skeleton published by NPHIES, so those facts are individually high-confidence. The structure as a whole is "medium" because (a) no official sample exists to check it against, (b) the skeleton is published without its signature and the signature's shape is unspecified, (c) the SSO flow around the message lives in two unreadable diagram images, and (d) one binding — Provider ID to saml:NameID — rests on a colour highlight rather than a sentence.
